long_biography.plain_text:
An imported-merchandise shop gave Hal Griffith his foothold on Seattle's waterfront. Renting warehouse space at Pier 57 in 1968, he opened Pirates Plunder and began planning a broader commercial reuse of the structure. When public plans threatened the old piers with clearance, he joined neighbouring businesses in pressing for preservation, while filling the building with shops and restaurants.

The site ultimately gave Griffith room to move beyond conventional property redevelopment. He had pursued an observation wheel for decades, but found the practical answer on the pier his enterprise controlled. The Seattle Great Wheel opened there in 2012, adding a major visitor attraction to the dining and retail mix. Municipal material still identifies Griffith as a waterfront pier and business owner.
